reason: Attacked on translation drift, which is this track's usual killer, and it holds. There are two quite different English renderings in circulation. The loose one, which Wikiquote carries as its banner line, reads "Hope is like a road in the country; there was never a road, but when many people walk on it, the road comes into existence"; it is not the Yangs and names no translator. The proposal does not blend the two, and that is the trap avoided. I downloaded the Lu Xun Internet Archive page myself and read the closing paragraph whole. It reads exactly as proposed, "I thought: hope cannot be said to exist, nor can it be said not to exist. It is just like roads across the earth. For actually the earth had no roads to begin with, but when many men pass one way, a road is made", and the page header credits "Selected Stories of Lu Hsun, Published by Foreign Languages Press, Peking, 1960, 1972", the named edition. The verifier's correction is right: the clause is "I thought: hope cannot be said to exist", with the verb kept and "hope" in lower case. I then pressed on the transcription itself, because that page is demonstrably noisy elsewhere in the story ("was nor in the least", "the same rime", "Jun-ru", "I hope they will not he like us"). So I fetched its upstream, coldbacon.com, which the page names as its transcription source, stripped the markup and read the same paragraph: it is identical to the proposal, character for character. The noise did not touch this passage. I also tried to open the printed volume and could not: the 1960 Foreign Languages Press Peking scan on the Internet Archive (selectedstorieso0000unse_b9d4) and the 1972 and 1978 printings are all access-restricted, and the full-text endpoints return 401. The verifier's declaration that no printed copy was opened is therefore accurate and stands; the attestation is two transcriptions of one lineage, both crediting the named volume. Attribution, locator and scope all check out: Lu Xun, "My Old Home" of 1921, the closing lines, a short story, tag Fiction, nothing needing a content warning, nothing after 1999. Not banned, not on the misattribution list, one of three for the year (month 1), and shipped.js returns no shipped or near match. Source line 110 characters, name first, no dash, curly quotes only, ends in a full stop. Not refuted. One small inconsistency is worth fixing rather than shipping: the source line romanises the translator as "Yang Xianyi" while the edition line, and the volume itself, print "Yang Hsien-yi". The rule asks for the translator of the published translation whose wording is used, so the source should match the volume.
